title: Retroductal Nanoparticle Injection to the Murine Submandibular Gland
protocol: Cut 3 cm of 32G intracranial catheter tubing with wire inset to form a beveled end at approximately 45° to the long axis.
Ensure the wire is at least 1 cm longer than the tubing.
Load 50 μL of PSMA nanoparticle solution into a Hamilton syringe.
Attach the catheter tubing, with the stylet removed, to the syringe and expel dead volume to reduce the probability of barotrauma during injection.
Inspect the injection solution to ensure the nanoparticle is fully solvated to prevent ductal obstruction following administration.
Prepare atropine solution at 0.1 mg/mL for the day of injection and protect it from light until administered.
Weigh C57/BL6 mice using an analytical balance.
Anesthetize mice with an intraperitoneally injected sterile saline solution containing 100 mg/kg ketamine and 10 mg/kg xylazine using a 0.5 mL syringe with 29G x ½" needle.
Proceed to the next step when the mouse no longer responds to stimuli, which generally occurs within 5 to 10 min following injection.
Apply lubricant to the eyes of the mouse.
Place the mouse in a prone position on a custom stage.
Secure the maxillary incisors over a metal beam.
Use an elastic band to apply downward tension behind the mandibular incisors.
Align the mouse beneath the dissecting microscope to visualize the base of the jaw.
Use a custom, curved steel retractor to apply tension bilaterally to the buccal mucosa to widen the mouth.
Grasp and gently lift the tongue from the floor of the mouth using blunt forceps.
Place cotton between the tongue and the buccal mucosa.
Grasp catheter tubing with fine, curved forceps.
Align the tubing with the curvature of the forceps for optimum manual control during cannulation.
Move the forceps and wire into the field of view using the dissecting microscope.
Gently apply pressure into the base of one submandibular papilla using the wire inset to produce a small, superficial, mucosal puncture (0.076 mm diameter).
Cut fresh beveled tips on both the tubing and wire inset with sharp dissecting scissors if resistance is encountered.
Withdraw the stylet after entry and confirm saliva presence at the puncture site under the dissecting microscope.
Avoid forceful or sudden movement of the stylet to prevent bleeding or ductal integrity compromise.
Retract the stylet within the tubing.
Insert tubing containing the stylet as a rigid guide into the previously made puncture.
Inspect for an opening visible under microscopy in the submandibular papilla.
If visible bleeding occurs, remove the stylet and reattempt from step 3.2 on the opposing submandibular papillae.
Administer intraperitoneal injection of 1 mg/kg atropine solution to reduce salivation during the procedure.
Wait 5 - 10 minutes after atropine administration.
Grasp the end of the syringe tubing.
Insert the tubing into the orifice using a dissecting microscope.
If resistance is encountered, cut a fresh beveled end to the tubing and reattempt insertion.
Once the tubing is in place within the submandibular papilla, slowly advance 3 - 5 mm into the duct.
Release the tubing from the forceps.
Dry the interface between the tubing and the submandibular papilla by gently blotting with gauze for 1 min.
Inspect to confirm that the position of the tubing has not shifted during drying.
Inject material at a rate of 10 µL/min.
Inspect to confirm that the mouse remains sedated and is not showing signs of distress.
Maintain syringe pressure for 5 min after injection to improve retention within Wharton's duct and SMG.
Inspect the submandibular papilla periodically during injection to ensure tubing does not exit the ductal orifice.
Using fine forceps, grasp and gently withdraw the tubing from the submandibular papillae.
Remove the retractor and cotton from the oral cavity before moving the mouse from the stage.
Do not leave the animal unattended until it has regained sufficient consciousness to maintain sternal recumbency.
Ensure that the mouse is not housed with other mice until fully recovered.
Use an in vivo Imaging System (IVIS) to assess retention of fluorescently labeled nanoparticles following injection.
Remove the ventral fur overlying the SMGs by shaving or using a chemical depilatory for better visualization.
Harvest SMG tissue following euthanasia and fix overnight in 4% paraformaldehyde.
Stain the fixed SMG tissue using immunohistochemistry to confirm persistence of fluorescently labeled NP one day following injection.
